Just before Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the decade-long development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentioned that former Apple CEO Tim Cook had participated in this project and revealed the possible pricing of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Cook returned from a business trip to China, he became "unusually excited" about foldable phones. According to reports, he pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable device.

Cook generally "does not participate in the conception of new products", so his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone gave this project more weight:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone (internally referred to by Apple as the iPhone Ultra), Apple's original entry-level target price was US$1,999. However, due to recent increases in component costs, the target price has been raised to US$2,199.

According to a source, Apple has discussed pricing its foldable product as high as US$2,199 in recent months, noting that various options have been considered recently, and the memory shortage has also significantly driven up Apple's cost targets. Some versions with larger storage capacities may be priced close to US$3,000. For comparison, the current standard iPhone starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra for the first time tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on site at the Steve Jobs Theater to bring you in-depth coverage of all the details.
